name: issue_748_manual_override_ends_whf_despite_rf_timer
description: Issue #748 (live incident 2026-08-22, reported as #739): a whole-house-fan session started via a QuietCool RF remote 1-hour timer, followed by the user manually setting the thermostat to cool, left the AC and the WHF running simultaneously for 5+ minutes. Issue #714's manual-override-conflict stand-down correctly detected the conflict and called _deactivate_fan(), but Issue #486's earlier 'RF remote timer is absolute' guard inside _deactivate_fan() silently declined the fan-off request — the two features were never reconciled.
notes: Occupant impact: the user runs the whole-house fan overnight via the RF remote's 1-hour timer button, then a few minutes later manually sets the thermostat to Cool at the wall. Without this fix, the AC and the whole-house fan both keep running — fighting each other, wasting energy, and violating the project's hard AC/WHF mutex invariant — for the rest of the RF timer's duration instead of the user's more recent action (the thermostat) winning immediately.

Fix (automation.py, Issue #748): added a bypass_absolute_override parameter to _deactivate_fan() that skips the Issue #486 RF-timer-absolute guard. Scoped to a single new shared helper, _stand_down_whf_for_override_conflict(), which replaced 4 previously-duplicated inline copies of the 'manual override conflicts with WHF -- stand it down' logic (immediate override detection, nat-vent-exit tick, nat-vent-temp-check tick, fan-thermostat-check tick). Only that helper passes bypass_absolute_override=True; every other _deactivate_fan() caller (routine automation shutoffs -- nat-vent cycling, bedtime, economizer-off, etc.) is untouched and still respects the RF-timer-absolute protection exactly as before.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: without the fix, _deactivate_fan() sees _fan_override_active=True and _fan_remote_timer_hours=1.0, logs 'Fan deactivation suppressed by active RF remote timer' and returns FanCommandResult.OVERRIDDEN without calling the fan-off service -- _fan_active stays True and this scenario's fan_not_active assertion fails, reproducing the exact live incident.

(b) Docs alignment: docs/grace-periods-spec.md documents the RF-remote-timer-absolute rule (Issue #486) and the manual-override-conflict stand-down rule (Issue #714) as separate sections; this fix's PR updates that doc to state the explicit precedence (hard AC/WHF mutex always wins over RF-timer-absolute protection) so the two sections no longer read as contradictory.

(c) User outcome if this scenario's assertion fails in the future: a WHF session started via an RF remote timer would once again be immune to the AC/WHF hard mutex for the remainder of the timer whenever the user manually changes the thermostat mode -- silently reverting to the Issue #739/#748 defect.

events.note: Seeds a real prior state for fan.whf -- the fan-entity listener requires both old_state and new_state to be non-None to evaluate a transition.
Matches the live incident: warm day, classification currently wants HVAC off (free cooling preferred).
Matches the live incident's indoor/outdoor readings at the time of the RF remote press.
User turns the whole-house fan on via the QuietCool RF remote's 1-hour timer button, matching the live incident's 15:00:18 press.

The RF remote's decoded firmware event: state is the press timestamp, attributes.event_type carries the selected 1-hour timer token. Real coordinator listener processes this and calls handle_fan_manual_override(duration_override=3600, remote_timer_hours=1.0, is_remote_event=True) -- setting _fan_override_active=True and _fan_remote_timer_hours=1.0, matching the live incident's 'RF remote timer: 1.0h' grace-start log line.

User manually sets the thermostat to Cool at the wall, matching the live incident's 15:00:58 override. Fires the real coordinator._async_thermostat_changed listener -> AutomationEngine.handle_manual_override() -> the WHF/nat-vent conflict stand-down.
A few minutes later -- long enough that a silently-suppressed fan-off (the live bug) would still show the WHF running at this point, exactly as it did in production through at least 15:05:52.

assertions.reason: The hard AC/WHF mutex must win over the RF-timer-absolute protection: once the user manually commands an active HVAC mode, the whole-house fan must be turned off immediately, even though its 1-hour RF remote timer has not expired. Reads the final _fan_active flag directly -- this is exactly the flag that stayed (wrongly) True in the live 2026-08-22 incident.

verdict.summary: After the Issue #748 fix, a manual thermostat override to an active mode immediately turns off a whole-house-fan session even when that session was started via an RF remote timer -- the hard AC/WHF mutex takes precedence over the Issue #486 RF-timer-absolute protection, which continues to apply normally to every other (non-conflicting) automation-driven fan shutoff.
verdict.observed_behavior: The WHF is commanded off immediately after the manual override to cool is detected, despite the active 1-hour RF remote timer -- _fan_active is False by 15:03:00.
verdict.expected_behavior: A manual override to an active HVAC mode must end an active WHF session immediately, regardless of any RF remote timer protecting that session from routine automation second-guessing -- last setting placed wins.
